messages:
Alex: heads-up — seeing a steady stream of tiny inference pods get evicted in eu-west1, then bounce to another AZ and die again. started ~16:00 UTC. looks like packing/hand-off is oscillating.
Priya: do you have a quick zap of logs? pod events or node pressure?
Alex: events show Prefetch eviction + NodeLostNetwork sporadic. sample: `Warning NodeNotReady kubelet has no status for 30s` then pods get descheduled.
Alex: log snippet: ```kubectl get events -n ml | grep preempt
2024-06-15T16:01:02 Evicted pod/app-xyz Preempted for higher priority
2024-06-15T16:01:09 Node/node-eu-west1b Warning NetworkUnstable NIC flapped 3x```
Mike: hmm, we've seen NIC flaps in eu-west1b earlier this month. autoscaler tries to backfill into the other AZ -> pack, then affinity/taint rules cause churn.
eng-scheduler-bot: autoscaler: scaled up +3 nodes in eu-west1a at 16:02 UTC (reason: pending-gpu-pods). Fallback routing enabled for gpu-small-tier.
Tara: could be the scheduler topology weight is still favoring AZ balance over node health. Suggest temporarily lowering azAffinity score for tiny-gpu class while we investigate.
Priya: low-risk immediate mitigation: cordon flaky nodes and drain pods to healthy pool, then set scheduler policy to avoid that AZ for 10m. commands: ```kubectl cordon node-eu-west1b-0 && kubectl drain node-eu-west1b-0 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```
Mike: long term we need two things: 1) detect NIC flaps as node unhealthy for scheduling decisions (treat as soft taint) 2) avoid reactive cross-AZ packing that causes tiny pods to bounce. also cost note — overprovisioning an extra warm pool in each AZ costs ~2.1k/mo but saves 10-15% evictions for these tiny workloads. tradeoffs? :thinking_face:
Alex: for now I cordoned the three worst nodes and set a temporary nodeSelector override for the tiny-tier to prefer eu-west1a. monitoring dashboard shows evictions dropping already. thanks team. :thumbsup:
